assets.researchSummary: Flare is moving from recovering after a security scare to selling its data network outside Flare. Issuer adoption of the DVN after its December launch is the evidence to watch.
assets.overview: Flare announced on Nov 12 that it will run a LayerZero verifier service (DVN) for cross-chain tokens from early December, starting with Flare and Ethereum: its 100 data providers confirm messages by stake-weighted majority, OFT issuers such as Tether, PayPal, Paxos and Ondo can add it, and each verification is paid in FLR with 90% of fees going to Flare's FIRE reinvestment entity. The same day Spectra's FXRP yield market gained an order book, and Firelight said it now backs vaults on Lido, Kraken and Sentora. This follows the clean Nov 11 activation of the emergency v1.15.1 hard fork after a Nov 10 exploit attempt on upstream node code, with no funds affected. On Nov 14 Flare shared DefiLlama Research's Firelight report, which puts active cover at $51.2 million across five vaults (Firelight is a DefiLlama Research client). On Nov 16 Firelight said higher protocol emissions lift staked-XRP yields to up to 4% APY, funded by cover fees rather than XRPL staking, and the value-locked alert has cleared at −14.8% over 7 days. The main risks are the missing post-mortem and whether issuers actually adopt the DVN.

assets.researchSummary: Distribution through 1inch and Coinbase options keeps growing while Hong Kong and the CFTC define the limits on access. Nov 21 brought no material Hyperliquid news; the XMR1 hack keeps issuer-key risk on permissionless spot listings in focus, and Wagyu's promised refunds have no published timeline.
assets.overview: Hyperliquid's growth case rests on a Hyperliquid Research Collective report (Nov 13) putting Q3 open interest at a record $16.8 billion with revenue up 22% to $191 million and stock-linked HIP-3 perpetuals up 161%. Distribution keeps widening: 1inch built Hyperliquid perpetuals into its app on Nov 19, and Coinbase Advanced added Deribit-powered HYPE options for eligible non-US users the same day. Regulators are pushing back on access, with Hong Kong's SFC flagging Hyperliquid as unlicensed on Nov 18 and CFTC Chairman Selig saying US retail access requires registering or partnering with a registered exchange; Hyperliquid has announced no US plan, while Kraken's Bitnomial route and Hyperliquid Strategies' FCM application are pending. On Nov 20 Wagyu confirmed that the $13.5 million collapse of its XMR1 token on Hyperliquid's spot book was a hack via a leaked deployer key, and pledged refunds; Hyperliquid's own chain was not compromised. The main risks are regulatory access limits, issuer-key risk on permissionless listings and speculative flows that may not last.

The material data issue is identity: CoinGecko still serves legacy aerodrome-finance separately from successor aero, while DefiLlama's aerodrome fees endpoint resolves to the broader Aero parent.
assets.overview: Aerodrome Finance began as a Base DEX, but the official upgrade hub says Aerodrome and Velodrome became the unified Aero protocol on October 21, 2026. The successor retains the AERO ticker, uses a new Base token contract and replaces legacy weekly voting with sAERO-based continuous reward allocation. Coinbase announced completed AERO/VELO conversion and restored sends and receives on November 6; Aero's November 8 post reiterates that completed exchange migration, rather than announcing another launch. Enso and Aero also confirmed access to the new MetaDEX's swaps, liquidity management and gauge staking across seven chains on November 6. The next evidence to track is successful migration, sustained routed usage and the relationship between actual pool revenue and reward issuance, not a newly verified dated upgrade in the next 60 days. Principal risks are migration and cross-chain contract dependencies, privileged emergency controls, ongoing issuance and mixing legacy Base-only statistics with successor-wide data.

assets.researchSummary: Bank tokenization keeps choosing Ethereum, now with UBS and HSBC products live in permissioned form. Glamsterdam has a tentative path, but the Nov 26 decision and the Sky outflows are the items to watch.
assets.overview: Ethereum drew two bank deployments on Nov 19: UBS used Chainlink's Runtime Environment to service a tokenized structured note on Ethereum in a production pilot, and HSBC opened a tokenized class of its Hong Kong-dollar money-market fund, recorded on Ethereum, to retail customers paying with its RedCoin stablecoin from HK$100. Both keep settlement or the official register off-chain and limit tokens to approved wallets. On the protocol side, the Nov 19 All Core Devs call leaned toward keeping Glamsterdam's EIP-8037 gas rules as written, pencilled the Hoodi testnet fork for Dec 16–17 and set a go/no-go for the Nov 26 consensus call; the EF says mainnet is no earlier than mid-January after outreach to at least 50 affected teams. Market-wide, Sky's USDS lost about 30% of its supply as $1.5 billion of USDC left its peg module after an illicit-flows report (peg held), and a $3.4 million exploit hit K3 Capital's sBOLD vault (Nov 18). The main risks are a further Glamsterdam slip and stress in large Ethereum DeFi stablecoins.

Its published Hayabusa model ties VTHO reward issuance to actively delegated VET, with VTHO used for gas and base fees burned; VET and VTHO therefore need separate treatment. A November 6 VeChain post highlighted Greencart's Kapok shopping agent and a developer-reported 250 Amazon orders in a week, with human approval retained. The key risk is mistaking rewarded consumer actions or agent demonstrations for durable paid demand, alongside validator-delegation concentration and application-security dependencies.

Its current ecosystem also includes XDC AI agent-payment infrastructure. Keyban's partner announcement, dated November 1 in its header and November 2 in its body, describes separate non-custodial agent accounts, USDC-per-call API payments and spending limits set by businesses. marketAlerts.change: Chainflip confirms about $12 million stolen from its Bitcoin and Ethereum vaults and offers the attacker a 10% bounty (escalated to High)
marketAlerts.summary: Chainflip Labs said in a message to the attacker on Nov 21 that 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3.25 million USDC and 758,141 USDT were taken from its vaults that day, adding a Bitcoin-vault loss to the roughly $4.86 million first traced on Ethereum; Cointelegraph puts the total at about $12 million. The Ethereum withdrawal carried a valid signature from the validators' shared vault key, and Chainflip says it has identified the mechanism of key exposure and blocked it, and traced a validator account registered on Nov 20. It offers the attacker 10% to return 90% by 18:38 UTC on Nov 23 (12:38 PM CST), after which it will pursue law enforcement. The protocol remains in safe mode with deposits, withdrawals and swaps disabled; cause details and a reimbursement plan have not been published.
marketAlerts.why: The confirmed loss now exceeds the $10 million High threshold, and Chainflip is a native cross-chain swap route between Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and other chains, so wallets using it on focus networks lose a path while it is halted. It is the second key-compromise incident in three days after XMR1 on Hyperliquid. Watch the Nov 23 bounty deadline.

marketAlerts.change: XMR1 collapse confirmed as a ~$13.5M hack: Wagyu says its deployer key leaked in a hosting-provider breach and pledges refunds (escalated to High)
marketAlerts.summary: Wagyu's pseudonymous founder PerpetualCow said on Nov 20 that the $13 million XMR1 sell-off on Hyperliquid's spot book was a hack: the token's deployer key sat on an old, deleted server at Icelandic host 1984.hosting, whose retained files were exposed in a breach. 1984 and Iceland's CERT-IS confirmed a serious cyberattack that forced the host to suspend all services, though their statement does not mention Wagyu. Bitquery and DefiLlama put the attacker's proceeds at about $13.5 million in USDC from roughly 370,000 XMR1 sold, converted to ETH and moved across Arbitrum and Ethereum, with most of the 5.2 million tokens still unsold. The founder says market makers took most losses, swap users lost nothing, and he will personally refund everyone who lost money, but gave no process or timeline; Wagyu is offline pending relaunch.
marketAlerts.why: The issuer now calls it a hack, which moves this from a suspected theft to a confirmed incident above the $10 million High threshold, and it happened on priority network Hyperliquid. Hyperliquid's own chain was not compromised; the lesson is issuer-key risk on permissionless HIP-1 spot listings. Watch whether refunds are actually paid.

marketAlerts.change: Cyber's LayerZero bridge drained of 5.21 million CYBER (~$1.1 million) after an unexpected mint on Solana; Upbit and Bithumb freeze transfers
marketAlerts.summary: Cyber, the social Layer 2 formerly called CyberConnect, said on Nov 21 it detected 'unexpected minting' of CYBER on Solana followed by a transfer out of its bridge's Ethereum lockbox. Onchain records cited by Upbit and The Block show 5,213,000 CYBER minted on Solana at 16:13 UTC (10:13 AM CST) and the same amount released from the Ethereum adapter two minutes later, nearly emptying it; most was sold for about 575 ETH, roughly $1 million. Upbit and Bithumb suspended CYBER deposits and withdrawals while trading continued. Cyber has not given a cause and asked users not to use the bridge or deposit CYBER to exchanges.
marketAlerts.why: The loss is small, but it is another bridge-configuration incident touching Solana and LayerZero routes, a pattern relevant to every multichain token on focus networks. The exploit was in Cyber's bridge setup, not in Solana itself.

marketAlerts.change: Kraken's Canadian-dollar markets dislocate for about 14 hours; bitcoin trades at C$24,250 and Kraken says trades stand
marketAlerts.summary: Kraken's Canadian-dollar order books, including BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, USDC, USDT and even USD/CAD, traded far below global prices from about 20:00 UTC on Nov 20 to 10:00 UTC on Nov 21 (2 PM Nov 20 to 4 AM Nov 21 CST). BTC/CAD printed as low as C$24,250 at about 08:00 UTC, roughly 71% below the US-dollar book converted at the Bank of Canada rate, while Kraken's BTC/USD pair stayed between about $55,100 and $59,400. Kraken Support said its systems worked as intended, found no security breach and that executed trades stand; it gave no cause. Public trade-tape analyses by CryptoSlate and Coindaro show large market sell orders arriving on a fixed schedule into thin books; who sent them is unknown.
marketAlerts.why: It is a reminder that local-currency books at top exchanges can be far thinner than headline pairs, and that market orders in thin weekend books can fill at extreme prices with no reversal. No funds were stolen and USD markets were unaffected, so it is Medium.

marketAlerts.change: Deribit halts trading for 19 minutes across perpetuals, options APIs and crypto transfers
marketAlerts.summary: Coinbase-owned derivatives exchange Deribit's status page said at 16:17 UTC on Nov 20 (10:17 AM CST) that trading was unavailable platform-wide, and at 16:36 UTC that trading had resumed, with the incident left under monitoring. Affected components included BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP perpetuals, stock-linked contracts, the FIX, REST and WebSocket APIs, and transfers of BTC, ETH, XRP and USDC on seven networks including Ethereum, Solana and Base. Earlier that day Deribit had applied a scheduled security patch with a planned pause of under five minutes. No cause for the afternoon outage was given.
marketAlerts.why: Deribit is the largest crypto options venue and, since Nov 19, the engine behind Coinbase Advanced's options for BTC, ETH, SOL, HYPE and XRP, so even short outages matter for hedging on focus assets. It was brief and no losses were reported, so it is Medium.

marketAlerts.change: Sky's USDS supply shrinks about 30% as $1.5 billion of USDC leaves its peg module after an illicit-flows report; peg holds
marketAlerts.summary: CoinDesk reported on Nov 19 that an Inca Digital investigation found about $518 million of transactions through Sky's Peg Stability Module (PSM) tied to hackers, sanctioned entities and other illicit wallets over several years, including more than $100 million attributed to North Korea. Because the PSM's USDC sits in one pooled address, a court-ordered freeze could immobilize the whole reserve. After the report more than $1.5 billion of USDC was withdrawn from the PSM, mostly by one large holder attributed to Poloniex, and USDS market capitalization fell more than 30% to about $3.2 billion while the token held its $1 peg. Sky founder Rune Christensen said USDS remains overcollateralized with about $10 billion of backing; separately, Sky's opt-in stUSDS lending pool is fully borrowed.
marketAlerts.why: USDS (formerly DAI) is one of the largest decentralized dollars and a core building block across Ethereum DeFi, so a run on its liquidity buffer matters for lending markets on Ethereum and other focus chains. The peg held, so this is a liquidity and compliance-risk event rather than a depeg, but the freeze risk on pooled stablecoin reserves applies well beyond Sky.

news.title: Chainflip's loss grows to about $12 million as its Bitcoin vault is hit too; it offers the attacker a 10% bounty
news.body: Cross-chain swap protocol Chainflip halted early on Nov 21 after 520 ETH, 3.25 million USDC and 758,000 USDT, about $4.86 million, left its Ethereum vault in one transaction signed with the validators' shared vault key. That evening Chainflip Labs published a message to the attacker listing 122.86 BTC as also taken, which Cointelegraph says brings the total to about $12 million. Chainflip says it has identified how the key was exposed and closed the hole, traced a validator account registered on Nov 20 and Tornado Cash funding from Nov 11, and will treat a 90% return by 18:38 UTC on Nov 23 (12:38 PM CST) as a white-hat recovery. The protocol remains in safe mode, and it has not published a technical post-mortem or a plan for affected users.
news.why: This is now an eight-figure, confirmed loss on a route wallets use to swap natively between Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana, lifting the market alert to High. Coming two days after the XMR1 key leak on Hyperliquid, it shows signing-key management, not contract code, is the recurring weak point this week.
news.tagReason: A confirmed $12 million key compromise halting a cross-chain route.

news.title: Kraken's Canadian-dollar books break from global prices for 14 hours, and Kraken lets the trades stand
news.body: From about 2 PM CST on Nov 20 to 4 AM CST on Nov 21, Kraken's Canadian-dollar markets for BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, the two dollar stablecoins and USD/CAD itself traded far below prices elsewhere. Bitcoin hit C$24,250, about 71% under Kraken's own US-dollar book at the Bank of Canada rate, before recovering above C$75,000 by about 3:48 AM CST. Kraken said its systems worked as intended, there was no breach, and executed trades stand, without giving a cause. Trade-tape analyses by CryptoSlate and Coindaro show about 28 large market sells arriving on a fixed hourly, then quarter-hourly, schedule into thin books; who placed them is not known.
news.why: It shows how thin local-currency books at a top exchange can be, and that fills at extreme prices are not reversed. No funds were lost to hacking and US-dollar markets were unaffected, so it is a Medium market-structure alert rather than an incident on any focus network.
news.tagReason: Venue-specific liquidity failure; no breach and no protocol impact.

news.title: Cyber's bridge loses 5.21 million CYBER after an unexpected mint on Solana; Korean exchanges freeze transfers
news.body: Cyber, formerly CyberConnect, said on Nov 21 it found 'unexpected minting' of CYBER on Solana followed by a transfer out of its bridge's Ethereum lockbox. Onchain records show 5,213,000 CYBER minted on Solana at 10:13 AM CST, sent back through the LayerZero route one minute later and released from the Ethereum adapter, which held almost exactly that amount; most was sold for about 575 ETH, roughly $1 million. Upbit and Bithumb suspended CYBER deposits and withdrawals while trading continued. Cyber has not identified the cause and asked users to stop using the bridge.
news.why: The dollar loss is small, but the mechanism, a mint accepted as a valid inbound bridge message, is a risk for any token bridged to Solana or elsewhere through a misconfigured route. Solana's protocol was not affected.
news.tagReason: Another bridge exploit, though small and app-level.

news.title: XMR1's $13.5 million collapse on Hyperliquid is confirmed as a hack; issuer Wagyu blames a hosting breach and promises refunds
news.body: Wagyu founder PerpetualCow said on Nov 20 that the overnight dump of XMR1, Wagyu's wrapped Monero token on Hyperliquid's spot book, came from a stolen deployer key: the key was on an old server at Icelandic host 1984.hosting that he had deleted, but the host's retained files were exposed when it was breached. 1984 and Iceland's CERT-IS separately confirmed a serious cyberattack that shut the host's services, although their statement does not mention Wagyu. Bitquery and DefiLlama put the attacker's take at about $13.5 million from roughly 370,000 of the 5.2 million tokens moved, with XMR1 falling from about $500 to $1 within half an hour. The founder says market makers bore most losses, swap users lost nothing, and he will refund everyone personally, but gave no timeline or claims process; Wagyu is offline until a relaunch.
news.why: Confirmation turns a suspected theft into a $13.5 million hack on a priority network, lifting the market alert to High. Hyperliquid's chain and its native XMR perpetual were unaffected, but the episode shows that permissionless spot listings inherit each issuer's key security, a point regulators already scrutinizing Hyperliquid may cite.
news.tagReason: A confirmed eight-figure hack on Hyperliquid's spot book, even though the chain itself held.

news.body: Hashi, Sui's native Bitcoin-finance infrastructure, went live on mainnet on Nov 19: deposited BTC stays on the Bitcoin network and an equal amount of hBTC is minted on Sui, secured by Sui's validators rather than a single custodian. Fluid's lending protocol launched on Sui at the same time and accepts hBTC as collateral for USDC loans, and HoneyB opened an hBTC vault and a USDC vault on Upshift. BitGo access and tri-party settlement are due in early 2027, and Ember's vaults later this year. Hashi went to testnet in July and partners had announced more than $500 million of capital commitments in October, when mainnet was first targeted.
news.why: Bitcoin is the largest pool of idle crypto capital, and a validator-secured route for it into Sui lending gives the network a new source of collateral and fee-generating activity. Delivery comes about a month after the original target, so the next test is how much BTC actually arrives and whether the committed institutional capital shows up.

news.title: Hong Kong publishes a bill to license crypto dealers, advisers, managers and custodians
news.body: Hong Kong's government gazetted the Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026 on Nov 20, extending the Securities and Futures Commission's licensing regime beyond trading platforms to virtual-asset dealing, advisory, management and custody services. Banks supervised by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and stored-value-facility licensees would have to register with the SFC to offer those services, and the bill adds fit-and-proper tests and penalties, including up to two years in jail for falsely claiming to be licensed. The Legislative Council's first reading is scheduled for Dec 2, and commencement dates are still to be set. It arrives two days after the SFC put Hyperliquid on its suspicious-platform list.
news.why: It fills gaps in one of Asia's main crypto hubs, so offshore venues and front ends serving Hong Kong users face a clearer licensing perimeter. Licensed custody and dealing rules matter for institutions distributing tokenized products on Ethereum, Solana and XRPL in the region. It is a bill, not law, until the Legislative Council passes it.
news.tagReason: Regulatory clarity with a long legislative path ahead.

news.title: Solana: storage deposits to fall ~7x within two weeks, and Anza sets 2027 capacity targets
news.body: On Nov 18 Solana said the deposit required to store data onchain ('rent') will fall about sevenfold within two weeks as the last three SIMD-0437 steps take it from 5,080 to 696 lamports per byte, each behind its own activation switch, citing Anza CEO Brennan Watt. Coverage on Nov 19 of Watt's Breakpoint roadmap set 2027 engineering targets: double benchmarked capacity to 500 million compute units per second, an 80% cut in compute for token-account transactions, onchain vector processing and 96 accounts per transaction instead of 64. These build on October's Alpenglow upgrade, which cut finality to a roughly 150-millisecond target. None of the rent steps has a fixed date, and the capacity goals run to end-2027.
news.why: Cheaper accounts and token transfers are what Breakpoint's payment and tokenization partners will need at scale. The rent steps are the near-term deliverable to verify; the 2027 numbers are targets, not shipped upgrades.
news.tagReason: A large near-term cost cut plus a dated capacity plan.

news.title: Ethereum developers lean toward keeping Glamsterdam's gas changes; Hoodi testnet pencilled for Dec 16–17, mainnet no earlier than mid-January
news.body: On the Nov 19 All Core Devs Execution call (ACDE #249), most execution-client teams (Geth, Nethermind, Reth and ethrex) favored shipping Glamsterdam with the EIP-8037 state-creation gas rules as written, while Erigon wants an amended specification and Besu still prefers one; no final decision was taken. Developers pencilled the Hoodi testnet fork for Dec 16 or 17, with the go/no-go moved to the consensus-layer call ACDC #192 on Nov 26, and supporters of a change have about a week to present a worked alternative. The Ethereum Foundation said its outreach with auditors ChainSecurity and Dedaub reached at least 50 affected teams; the three high-severity cases are fixed or will be by mid-December. That points to mid-January as the earliest mainnet date, with the call's chair calling late January or early February more realistic.
news.why: Glamsterdam carries Ethereum's next base-layer scaling step, and this gives the first realistic timeline since the Nov 16 warning that up to 15,000 contracts could break. A Nov 26 'no' would push the choice into January, so that call decides whether the upgrade slips further.
news.tagReason: A tentative path forward, but no decision yet and mainnet is at least two months out.

news.title: Bittensor switches on post-quantum wallets, then ships runtime 492 to harden key swaps
news.body: TAO Media reported on Nov 18 that Bittensor's post-quantum account support, deployed in runtime 488 on Nov 5, is now enabled: ML-DSA-65 and Falcon-512/1024 wallets can register and sign transactions, and hashed accounts rotate signing keys after each transaction, while existing Sr25519 and Ed25519 wallets need no migration. On Nov 19 runtime 492 went live on Finney with six fixes, mostly to coldkey and hotkey swaps: destination wallets keep their own settings, conflicting lock settings are rejected before a fee is charged, and elevated 'Operational' priority is limited to sudo-signed calls. Fees, storage and transaction weights are unchanged. Users still need compatible wallet software for post-quantum accounts.
news.why: Bittensor is among the first large networks to let holders opt into post-quantum signatures on mainnet, and safer key swaps reduce custody risk for holders and subnet operators. Both are security capabilities rather than economic changes, so uptake is what to watch.
news.tagReason: Security hardening with no economic changes.

news.title: NEAR details SHIELD, a screening layer that keeps hack proceeds out of NEAR Intents without pausing the chain
news.body: NEAR published details on Nov 19 of SHIELD, the financial-integrity layer for NEAR Intents that screens incoming funds by their public onchain history before execution and declines flagged requests, without KYC and without touching balances on the NEAR base layer. NEAR says SHIELD blocked 99.7% (more than $50 million) of laundering attempts after September's Bitget hack and, as of Nov 3, about 96% of Binance-exploit-linked flows that reached NEAR Intents. It runs three modes, Normal, Paranoid and Under Attack, with scoped controls by chain, bridge, token or address, and NEAR is inviting wallets, bridges and exchanges to contribute incident data. The blocking figures are NEAR's own and were not independently audited.
news.why: Cross-chain swap venues are a main route for laundering stolen funds, so a documented screening layer helps NEAR Intents stay usable for institutions and exchanges. It also draws a clear line between a permissionless base chain and app-level policy, which regulators are watching.
news.tagReason: Security infrastructure with self-reported results.

news.title: Nvidia brings Vera Rubin systems to Azure at Ignite, and California's attorney general subpoenas it in a China chip probe
news.body: At Microsoft Ignite on Nov 19 Nvidia said Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are running in Azure with wider virtual-machine access, its Nemotron 3.5 models and customization tools are available in Microsoft Foundry, and Azure Local gains RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and Jetson options. The same day CNBC reported that California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia as part of an investigation tied to chip sales to China. Nvidia had not detailed its response in the report.
news.why: Vera Rubin in a major cloud is the next product cycle after Blackwell reaching customers, supporting the demand Nvidia guided to on Nov 17. A state-level probe adds to the federal export-control scrutiny around China sales.
news.tagReason: New platform in Azure offset by a new legal inquiry.

news.title: Google opens Genie 4 to developers through the Gemini API and ships Gemini computer use for Mac
news.body: Google made Genie 4, its interactive world-generation model, available through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio on Nov 19, letting developers generate interactive 720p worlds with synchronized audio and real-time controls. It also previewed Tool Retrieval for the Gemini Interactions API, which loads tool definitions on demand so agents can scale to many tools, and launched Gemini computer use on Mac to automate multi-step tasks across apps, files and websites. Google also announced a heavy-lift launch partnership with Blue Origin for Project Suncatcher, its space-based AI compute research.
news.why: Opening Genie 4 and agent tooling to developers a day after Gemini 4 Neon extends Google's push to make its models the default platform for agent builders, which feeds Google Cloud revenue. Suncatcher remains a long-dated research effort.
news.tagReason: New developer access to frontier models and agent tools.

news.body: Meta released its 2026 Sustainability Report on Nov 19 and said it is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero target as its AI infrastructure build-out grows, with Axios reporting a 45% rise in AI-related emissions. The same day Meta let Quest 3 and 3S users in the US rent and buy 3D movies through the TV app, with more than 150 titles. It also premiered an anti-scam microdrama series with the Indian government.
news.why: Walking back a flagship climate target shows how much energy Meta's AI capex requires, which adds to scrutiny of its data-center spending. The Quest content move is small but supports engagement on its VR hardware.
news.tagReason: A climate commitment under review because of AI energy demand.

news.title: Intel says 18A yields have reached about 70%
news.body: Following Nov 18's news of a first external 18A-P customer and Microsoft's EMIB packaging and Xeon commitments, Tom's Hardware reported on Nov 19 that Intel puts yields on its 18A process at about 70%. Microsoft's agreement covers multi-year Xeon supply including next-generation Diamond Rapids CPUs. The external 18A-P customer remains unnamed.
news.why: Yield is what decides whether 18A can be profitable for Intel and credible to outside foundry customers, so a 70% figure supports the turnaround narrative. It is a company-reported number without independent verification.
news.tagReason: Improving yields on the process that underpins the foundry plan.

It also highlighted Cohere Compass, Cohere's enterprise search and retrieval system, running on AMD infrastructure, and FastFlow adding a GPU execution path on AMD hardware.
news.why: Software support is the main gap between AMD's AI PC and data-center chips and Nvidia's ecosystem, so each developer integration helps. These are ecosystem announcements rather than revenue disclosures.

weeklyRecap.title: Week in context · Nov 4–10, 2026
weeklyRecap.body:
The week's main theme was distribution moving into regulated and mainstream channels. Solana gained Formation's SEC-exemption notice for a tokenized-securities venue, a Schwab Crypto listing, a native privacy layer from Helius and one-tap trading from X cashtags; NEAR Intents went live in Talos's institutional system; HYPE gained won markets on Upbit and Bithumb plus the Elysium L2; and Ondo brought Fidelity's FCAT into every tokenized-stock bridge transfer. Bittensor's Gamma Tokens went live as a protocol payment rail, though first-day use was tiny.

Governance moved from votes to execution. Polkadot enacted Referendum 1966's 500-validator target on Nov 10, while Acala and Karura proposed shutting down in February 2027. Render's RNP-024 closed with only yes votes shown but no official announcement, and the XRPL Foundation's quantum-safe account design remains a draft with a 2027 study.

Security is the cross-watchlist caution. Flare forced an emergency hard fork after an exploit attempt, NEAR AI contained a cloud intrusion, and Elliptic traced Binance-hack laundering through NEAR memecoins. Market-wide incidents at Keplr/Web3Auth, LNbits, Ankr, Arcus, Initia and Across were each below the High threshold. Nothing in this recap is a price forecast or financial advice.

stocks.name: Tesla, Inc.
stocks.overview: Tesla builds electric vehicles and energy-storage systems and is investing heavily in self-driving (FSD, Robotaxi and the Cybercab), Optimus robots and its own AI compute. In Q3 2026 revenue was $28.05 billion, roughly flat year over year, with 486,532 deliveries (down about 2%) and net income attributable to common stockholders of $787 million ($0.22 per diluted share), down from $1.37 billion a year earlier; energy revenue fell 16% while services and other rose 33%. Recent moves include Cybercab service starting in Austin in September, a new €100 million Berlin engineering center that opened Nov 4 with about 250 staff, and an official Argentina launch set for Nov 20. Shareholders meet on Dec 3, and Tesla and SpaceX have discussed a possible combination, though no terms have been announced and any deal would need shareholder approval. The main near-term risk is political: after Democrats won Congress and Texas, Tesla and SpaceX shares fell about 11% and 9% on Nov 5, as investors priced in possible congressional probes and tighter rules on AI data centers.

Market expansion in Argentina and a provisional Italian approval contrast with a South Korean rejection, so approvals remain country by country.

Capital expenditures were $34.91 billion in the quarter and free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion. Meta expects 2026 capex of $135–145 billion and Q4 revenue of $73–76 billion. To fund the AI build-out it sold $15 billion of US-dollar bonds on Nov 3 and its first euro bonds (€9 billion) on Nov 4, and it has announced a non-voting Class C share class effective Jan 19, 2027. Product momentum in Muse continues, while litigation and data-center permitting after the midterms are the main watch items.

stocks.overview: Alphabet owns Google Search, YouTube, Android, Google Cloud and the Gemini AI models, and sells its TPU AI chips through Google Cloud. This week Google announced a $15 billion data-center investment in Malaysia for 2027–2028 (Nov 4) and a $17 billion first data center in Laramie County, Wyoming (Nov 5), powered partly by a 702 MW Bloom fuel-cell system with carbon capture. Alphabet pays a $0.22 quarterly dividend on Dec 14 to holders of record on Dec 7. The main risk is legal: appeals are pending in both U.S. antitrust cases (search and ad tech), and a court refused to pause related private ad-tech suits.

Jones became the board's first chair, and the board is searching internal and external candidates. In Q2 fiscal 2027 (to July 26, 2026) revenue rose 106% to $96.2 billion with data center revenue of $89.0 billion, and Nvidia guided Q3 revenue to $108.0 billion ±2%, assuming no data-center compute revenue from China. On Nov 17 it reported Q3 fiscal 2027 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103%, with data-center revenue of $107.6 billion, guided Q4 to $130 billion ±3% (including an extra week and again no China data-center compute), and said Vera Rubin NVL72 systems have shipped.
